title: The Three-Body Problem
author: Liu, Cixin
review:
Even though this has some rough edges, this is one of the best sci-fi books I've read and the ideas explored here are mind blowing.

This is probably the "hardest" sci-fi book I've read where Liu goes deep into the physics and some of the technical details about why the things explored here might be possible. I personally loved this aspect of the book but I could see it causing issues for others.

At times it feels like reading physics proofs and theorems, but in a dramatized way, he also takes interesting applications of computer science concepts that were pretty unexpected to me and that I appreciated a lot.

This book gets criticized for the thin characters which I think overall is fair; it definitely focuses on the ideas and sci-fi concepts, but I didn't think that the characters were poorly written, a couple are interesting and even funny. He definitely sort of puts this on the side about halfway through the book and focuses primarily on the ideas, which I'm ok with.

Really looking forward to the next two books as I've heard they're even better. I'm really glad to have read this and kind of mad at myself for waiting so long. Definitely a unique style of sci-fi that is sort of a more technical version of Clarke in a lot of ways. Can't say I've read anything quite like this even though it uses familiar sci-fi concepts, the way they are blended together and executed is really interesting.
